limits: Windows normal shell startup only; no managed-launcher, POSIX, reset-as-contender or key-command-as-contender coverage.
Reset overlap is established by a timing precondition using 2,500 disposable files.
Stack detection and actionable-guidance checks are pattern based. Holder identity is generic, not specifically a reset.
Six informational assertions are reported separately and do not determine the verdict.
No broad process inventory; driver children exited normally. Two early older-driver attempts were discarded by the QA author.

reconstructedBaseline.kind: Controlled reconstruction, separate from the independently executed signed baseline
reconstructedBaseline.purpose: Reconstructed main-equivalent API build for #409 baseline QA (not a product build)
reconstructedBaseline.method: Candidate build with the two runtime-changed modules replaced by transpiled source from base; transpiling candidate modules reproduced their built bytes. The temporary reconstructed tree was removed by QA.

observations: All 14 scenarios and 137 assertions pass twice on candidate. Reconstructed baseline has 104/137 passes and 33 refusal-shape failures; all its positive cases and unrelated-error controls pass.
Actual reset holder is established by PID/lock and continued liveness after refusal. It completes normally; subsequent normal startup passes.
Guidance identifies another GraphGoblin process generically, not a reset or PID. Windows refusal takes approximately 3.5 to 5 seconds for existing identity checks.
limits: Windows shell startup only. Managed launcher, key-command holder, reclamation-guard holder, permission-denied identity checks, WMI timeout and database hardlink case not run.
Holder release uses owned API shutdown or reset completion, not OS signals. Reset timing uses 3,000 disposable files and validates overlap.
Two smoke calibrations used an earlier driver and are not counted. Repository test suites were not run by this independent QA context.
Retained driver bytes are hashed after terminal; the raw candidate JSON names the driver but does not embed its SHA-256.
